changes: Added a host-neutral retired-root/canonical-root guard to Lattice CLI, documented Orchestrate as a read-only legacy evidence root, recorded B-3523/B-fbb6 migration recovery paths, and configured old Orchestrate to point writes to proofbound.
usage: Use /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound for all new Lattice work. The old /Users/jek/Documents/Work/Orchestrate root can still run read-only inspection commands, but mutating commands now fail before handler dispatch and print the proofbound canonicalRoot.
expectedOutcome: Agents and hosts can no longer accidentally create or mutate stories in the retired Orchestrate checkout; legacy evidence remains readable locally, and B-3523/B-fbb6 are recoverable from proofbound .worktrees.
actualTranscript: Read-only Orchestrate session_brief succeeded. A story_create attempt against Orchestrate exited nonzero and printed `Lattice root is retired: /Users/jek/Documents/Work/Orchestrate` and `Use canonicalRoot: /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound`. B-3523 and B-fbb6 directories exist under proofbound .worktrees, and Orchestrate has no active story/B-3523 or story/B-fbb6 worktree/branch entries. Validate passed 25/25 configured commands and DONE-required validation passed packages/main build plus root full test suite.
outcomeDiff: Expected and actual behavior match for migration safety: the retired root is readable but not writable, and the failure path gives the canonical proofbound recovery command target. Remaining Orchestrate lab/temp worktrees are separate legacy artifacts, not active migrated B-3523/B-fbb6 story worktrees.
limitations: This story does not normalize, rebase, finish, or merge B-3523/B-fbb6 business work; it preserves them under proofbound. It also does not delete remaining Orchestrate lab/temp worktrees or unrelated local experiment files.
pitfalls: The guard only activates when a root config declares retiredRoot true with canonicalRoot. The proofbound CLI code and the old Orchestrate local config both matter; changing only one side would leave either no enforcement or no activation.
